name: Table
purpose: Present a large, sortable, filterable set of records - the workhorse of list/index ("All X") pages.
intent: A data-table shell: a section header (title + description), a toolbar (search + filter/configure icon buttons + actions + active-filter Chip mode='filter' pills), a column-config-driven grid (sortable headers, a selection column, row/loading/empty states), and a pagination footer. Driven by `columns` + `data`; sorting, selection, and search are owned by default (uncontrolled) with controlled overrides, and pagination is client-side or server-driven. Composes Text Field, Select, Checkbox, Icon Button, Button, and Skeleton (and hosts consumer-rendered Chips) into one complete section - which is why it lives at the organism tier.
nativeElement: table (semantic thead/tbody/th/td, with a visually-hidden caption)

figmaSource.note: Not a variant set: the `table` frame (2949:40357) holds two size components - size=md (2949:40355) and size=sm (2949:40356). The Figma page is marked in-progress (✅⏲️), and the grid renders empty in the master because its cells live in the separate 'Parts' library (a `figma-parts / column / <type>` per cell content type). Verified live via figma-dev-mode.

subParts.name: table / head
subParts.note: The section header: {title} (heading/lg), {description} (body/md, content/subtle), and a right-aligned button-group of two Buttons + an overflow Icon Button. Maps to the `title` / `description` / `actions` props.

subParts.name: table / filters
subParts.note: The toolbar: a search Text Field (left, flex-growing up to 600px) + filter/configure Icon Buttons (right), a row of Chip mode='filter' active-filter pills + a '+' add-filter Icon Button + a 'Clear all filters' action (right), over a bottom border separator. Code maps this to search (`searchable`) + `toolbarActions` (Icon Buttons) + `activeFilters` (consumer-rendered Chip mode='filter' ReactNode) + `onClearFilters`. The filter/configure dropdowns are consumer-owned.

subParts.name: table / columns
subParts.note: The grid, laid out column-by-column: a 24px left/right gutter (`column / padding`), up to 8 (wide) or 16 (narrow) column slots, and vertical/horizontal scrollbars. In code this is a normal row-oriented <table>; the per-column layout is expressed as the `columns` config.

subParts.name: cell / table-head
subParts.note: The header cell (deep-verified via the Desktop Bridge): background elevation/surface/sunken on each header cell (a subtle grey band vs. the white body rows), a Title label in heading/xs SemiBold coloured content/SUBTLE (not default), an always-visible sort Icon Button (arrow_down) + a column-menu (⋮) dropdown, a vertical drag-handle divider (border/default) between columns, and a bottom border (border/default). Header height 40 (md) / 32 (sm). Code renders the sort control (asc/desc/none, with aria-sort; the arrow stays visible and takes content/default when active) and defers the column-menu ⋮ and drag-resize to future work.

subParts.name: cell / text (and 20+ other cell types)
subParts.note: Body cell (deep-verified): content at --spacing-sm inline padding, body/md, content/default, transparent background, with a bottom row divider (--color-border-default). Row height 64 (md) / 40 (sm). Figma ships a `column / <type>` for each cell content type; the code does NOT hard-code these - a column's `render` returns any content composed from existing atoms/molecules (see cellContentTypes).

subParts.name: container-pagination
subParts.note: The footer: the Pagination molecule, centered, over a top border.

figmaSource.cellContentTypesNote: The Figma cell content types the grid is designed to hold (from the 'Parts' `figma-parts / column / <type>` list, verified live 2026-09-10). The code expresses these through a column's `render` prop rather than one component per type; a built-in selection Checkbox column is the exception.
apiAdaptationNotes: Column-config driven, not slot-composed. Figma lays the grid out as columns, each a stack of a header cell + body cells of one content type; the code takes `columns` (with `key`, `header`, `sortable`, `align`, `width`, `render`) + `data` and renders a semantic row-oriented <table>. This scales to a data-heavy app (many similar 'All X' pages) far better than hand-composed rows.

Cells render arbitrary content via `column.render` rather than a component-per-content-type. Figma's 20+ `column / <type>` parts are examples of what a cell can hold (Tag, Avatar, Link, Badge, Button, ...); baking a renderer for each would be a combinatorial, low-value surface. The one structural exception is the selection Checkbox column (`selectable`).

Batteries-included but controllable. Sorting and selection are owned by default (uncontrolled: `defaultSort` / `defaultSelectedIds`) with controlled overrides (`sort`+`onSortChange`, `selectedIds`+`onSelectionChange`). The built-in sort reorders `data` client-side; `manualSort` hands sorting to the consumer (server-side).

Pagination is controlled or client-side. Pass `pageSize` for client-side slicing (the table computes the page count and owns the page), or `manualPagination` + `page`/`pageCount`/`onPageChange` for server-driven paging. Search text is uncontrolled by default (`defaultSearchValue`) or controlled (`searchValue`); either way `onSearchChange` reports it and the consumer owns the data query.

The toolbar renders the shell (search + `toolbarActions` Icon Buttons + active-filter Chip mode='filter' pills + Clear filters); the filter/configure dropdowns are consumer-owned, since specific filter categories do not generalise. Pass `toolbar` to replace the built-in toolbar entirely.

Accessibility: a real <table> with a visually-hidden <caption> (or the `title`) for the accessible name; each header cell is named by its label alone (aria-labelledby its label, or aria-label = headerLabel); sortable headers set aria-sort and wrap the label in a <button> named by the same label; the scroll region is a keyboard-focusable role=region; `aria-busy` marks the loading state.

Token fidelity was confirmed via the Desktop Bridge deep read (resolving boundVariables to token names): header cell background = elevation/surface/sunken (on each cell, which a sticky header needs), header text = content/subtle, cell text = content/default, all borders/dividers = border/default. The row HOVER and SELECTED backgrounds are not specified in the (in-progress ⏲️) Figma page, so they use inferred semantic tokens (neutral-overlay-subtle-hover / brand-primary-subtle) - revisit them when the design specifies row states.

Deferred from v1 (Figma page is in-progress): single-select (radio) column, the per-column ⋮ menu, column resize/reorder, sticky first column, and row expansion. The sortable header + selection Checkbox cover the primary interactions.

useCases: an 'All members' / 'All records' list page with search, filters, sorting, and pagination
a selectable list with bulk actions (select-all + per-row checkboxes)
a compact dense table (size='sm') for data-heavy views
a server-driven table (manualSort + manualPagination) backed by a paged API
antiPatterns: a simple key/value layout or a short static list (use a description list or plain markup)
a layout grid / dashboard of cards (use layout primitives, not a data table)
editable spreadsheet-style grids with cell-level editing and formulas (out of scope)

anatomy.description: Flex column holding the header and the table body. Fills its container's width.
Rendered when there's a title or description: the title (heading/lg at md, heading/md at sm), a heading at headingLevel (h2 by default), over a description (body/md, content/subtle).
Holds the toolbar, the grid's scroll region, and the footer, with no border or radius. data-has-footer marks whether the pagination footer is shown.

Rendered for `toolbar`, `searchable`, `toolbarActions`, `actions`, `onClearFilters`, `activeFilters`, or a selection. Row 1: a right-aligned button group (search, then `toolbarActions`, then `actions`), or the selection bar while rows are selected. Row 2: `activeFilters` and the Clear filters button. `toolbar` replaces both rows.
Shown while one or more rows are selected, in place of the toolbar's button group: the selected count, then `bulkActions`, on the selected background with a selected border.
The scrollable, keyboard-focusable region around the <table>, named by a string caption or title (or scrollRegionLabel, 'Table'). Its top border separates the grid from the toolbar.
Semantic table with a visually-hidden <caption> for its accessible name; aria-busy while loading.

anatomy.element: th (scope=col, aria-sort, aria-labelledby its label or aria-label = headerLabel)
anatomy.description: Sticky header cell (elevation/surface/sunken background, content/subtle heading/xs), named by its label alone; sortable columns wrap the label and sort arrow in a <button> named by the same label.

Drag handle at the header cell's trailing edge; resizes the column by pointer drag or ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, between 64px and the scroll region's width, and reports the width from the first render. Named by getResizeLabel. Shown when resizableColumns and column.resizable !== false.
Leading column with a header select-all Checkbox and a per-row Checkbox; shown when `selectable`. Selection is checkbox-only - rows are never clickable.
Body row with a bottom divider on its cells (dropped for a lone row, or the last row when there's no footer). Every row has a neutral-overlay hover; a selected row is brand-tinted.
Body cell; body/md (heading weight when column.emphasis='strong'); renders `column.render(row)` or `String(row[key])`. An editable cell's control fills it.

Pagination footer, shown when there's more than one page or itemsPerPageOptions is set: the items-per-page Select (named by its visible label) and range text on the left, the page Select, page count, and previous/next Icon Buttons on the right, over a top border.

columns.description: Column definitions (key, header, render, sortable, align, width, resizable, emphasis, ...). column.resizable=false opts a column out of resizing; column.emphasis='strong' marks an identifier column (heading weight).

data.description: The row data. Sorted/paginated unless the matching manual flag is set.

getRowId.description: Stable row id for selection and React keys. Pass a real id when using selection.

size.description: Row density and title size: md (64px rows, a heading/lg title) or sm (40px rows, a heading/md title).

caption.description: Accessible name for the <table> (visually-hidden caption). Falls back to `title`.

title.description: A section heading labelling the table among other content (heading/lg at md, heading/md at sm), rendered at headingLevel. A page that's only a table uses the page header and leaves it out. Names the table when there's no caption.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of title, to fit the page's outline. Only the outline: the size follows size.

actions.description: Actions such as a primary Button, at the end of the toolbar's button group after toolbarActions. Hidden while rows are selected.

toolbar.description: Replaces the entire built-in toolbar, including search, actions, active filters, and the selection bar.

searchValue.description: Controlled search text. Without it, Table keeps the text itself.

defaultSearchValue.description: The search text to start with when searchValue isn't controlled; the field starts open when it isn't empty.

onSearchChange.description: Called with the new search text as the person types, and with '' when they clear it. Controlled or not.

searchPlaceholder.description: Search field placeholder. Not used as its accessible name.

searchLabel.description: Accessible name for the search field and the Icon Button that opens it.

clearSearchLabel.description: Accessible name for the search field's clear button.

toolbarActions.description: Right-aligned toolbar actions beside the search field — typically a filter Icon Button and a configure Icon Button. The consumer owns the buttons and their dropdown/popover content.

activeFilters.description: Applied filters rendered below the search row. Pass a Chip Group named with aria-label ("Active filters") holding Chip mode='filter' components, so the set is announced and focus stays in the group when a chip is removed. Table lays the row out but doesn't wrap it in a group (a consumer's group would be nested in a second one). The consumer renders and controls the chips.

onClearFilters.description: When set, renders a Clear filters button at the trailing edge of the active-filters row.

manualSort.description: Consumer sorts server-side; Table reflects state but does not reorder data.

selectable.description: Enable the leading selection Checkbox column + header select-all.

getSelectionLabel.description: Accessible name for a row's selection Checkbox, from the row, such as 'Select Ada Lovelace'. Pass it: the default names every row the same.

bulkActions.description: Actions shown on the right of the selection bar when one or more rows are selected.

selectionCountLabel.description: Formats the selection-bar count, which a polite live region also announces when it changes (not on the first render).

page.description: Controlled current page (1-based). Table never changes it: set it back to 1 when the search or a filter changes data. Uncontrolled, with client-side paging, the page goes back to 1 when the rows in data become a different set of ids.

pageSize.description: Rows per page; enables client-side pagination. With manualPagination it places the range text (without it, the rows passed count as one page).

manualPagination.description: Consumer paginates server-side; Table shows pageCount pages and does not slice.

previousPageLabel.description: Accessible name for the footer's previous-page button.

nextPageLabel.description: Accessible name for the footer's next-page button.

paginationLabel.description: Accessible name for the footer's navigation region, as given. Wins over getPaginationLabel.

getPaginationLabel.description: Accessible name for the footer's navigation region, from the table's name (a string caption or title).

itemsPerPageLabel.description: The footer's page-size label, shown as given (Table adds no colon), which also names its Select.

getRangeLabel.type: (start: number, end: number, total: number) => string
getRangeLabel.description: The footer's range text, from the page's first and last row shown and the total (0–0 with no rows).

pageLabel.description: Accessible name for the footer's page Select.

getPageCountLabel.description: The text after the footer's page Select.

resizableColumns.description: Allow dragging column-header edges (and Arrow keys on the handle) to resize columns.

getResizeLabel.description: Accessible name for a column's resize handle.

empty.default: emptyLabel, transparent on the table's surface
empty.description: Shown when there are no rows, such as an Empty State that says why and what to do next.

emptyLabel.description: The default empty content: one neutral statement, true whether nothing exists yet or a search found nothing.

emptyHeadingLabel.description: Deprecated - use emptyLabel (renamed: the default empty content is one statement, not a heading). Still accepted, and rendered the same; an explicit emptyLabel wins.

emptyDescriptionLabel.description: Deprecated - the default empty content is one statement, emptyLabel. Still accepted, and shown under emptyLabel; for a heading and description, pass an Empty State as empty.

getResultCountLabel.description: The result count (totalItems, else data.length), announced politely when it changes after the first render, as after a search or filter. Not announced while loading.

scrollRegionLabel.description: Accessible name for the scroll region when neither caption nor title is a string.

className.description: Composes with the root class list.

slots.name: columns[].render
supports: arbitrary cell content - Text, Tag, Avatar, Avatar Group, Link, Badge, Button, Icon Button, Progress Bar, Toggle, inline editors, ...

slots.name: activeFilters
supports: Chip Group (named with aria-label) of Chip mode='filter'

color.resizeHandleDivider: --color-border-default 1px (default) → --color-border-bold 1px (hover/pressed); handle width stays 1px in all states

requirements: A semantic <table> with thead/tbody/th(scope=col)/td and a visually-hidden <caption> (or the title) as the accessible name - always give it a name.
Each column header is named by its label alone (not the controls inside it). Sortable headers set aria-sort (ascending/descending/none) and wrap the label in a <button> named by the same label.

One polite live region, silent on the first render: when the result count (totalItems, else data.length) changes, as after a search or filter, it announces getResultCountLabel(count) ('No results', '12 results'; not while loading); when the selected count changes, selectionCountLabel(count). The result count wins when both change at once.

The selection column uses real Checkboxes; the header select-all is labelled and goes indeterminate when only some visible rows are selected. Selection is checkbox-only - rows are never clickable, so controls inside a row act independently.

Column resize handles are role=separator (aria-orientation=vertical), keyboard-focusable, operable with Arrow keys, and report aria-valuenow (the width in px), aria-valuemin (64), and aria-valuemax (the scroll region's width) from the first render.
The scrollable grid is a keyboard-focusable role=region with an accessible name (WCAG 2.1.1).
The loading state sets aria-busy on the table; skeletons are decorative.
Row content composed via render must remain accessible (e.g. give action buttons labels).

keyboardInteraction: Tab reaches the toolbar controls, the scroll region, the sortable header buttons and resize handles, the selection checkboxes, in-cell controls, and the footer controls, in that order.
Enter/Space on a sortable header button cycles the sort (ascending → descending → unsorted).
Space toggles a selection checkbox (a native checkbox); the header checkbox toggles all visible rows.
A focused column resize handle resizes with ArrowLeft / ArrowRight.
The scroll region is focusable so it can be scrolled by keyboard.
behaviorRules: Render the grid from `columns` + `data`; a cell shows `column.render(row)` or `String(row[key])`.
Sorting is uncontrolled by default (defaultSort) and controlled via sort+onSortChange; the built-in sort reorders data client-side unless manualSort.
Sort cycles ascending → descending → unsorted per column.

Selection is checkbox-only (rows are never clickable), uncontrolled by default (defaultSelectedIds) and controlled via selectedIds+onSelectionChange; select-all operates over the visible (current-page) rows.
When one or more rows are selected, the selection bar (selected count + bulkActions) replaces the toolbar's button group (search, toolbarActions, actions). The column headers stay.

Selection is kept by id across pages, sorts, and filters (decided): a selected row that a filter now hides stays selected, the selection count includes it, and bulk actions act on every selected id. A bulk action's confirmation names the count it will act on.

All rows show a neutral-overlay-bold hover (aids horizontal scanning); the selected state is brand-tinted. A single row - or the last row when there is no pagination footer - drops its bottom divider.

Columns are resizable by default (resizableColumns): drag the header-edge separator or use Arrow keys; per-column opt-out via column.resizable=false. The first resize freezes every column's width (fixed table-layout) so a resize doesn't reflow the others and the widths persist across page/data changes.
column.emphasis='strong' renders a cell at the heading weight (an identifier); otherwise body weight.
Pagination is client-side when pageSize is set (Table slices + owns the page) or server-driven when manualPagination (Table shows pageCount pages).

A new result set starts from the first page: with client-side paging and no page prop, Table goes back to page 1 when the rows in data become a different set of ids (rows added or removed, as a search or filter does); editing or reordering rows keeps the page. A controlled page, and the page with manualPagination, are never changed: the consumer resets them.

loading shows skeleton rows and sets aria-busy; skeletons sit where their column's content does (align center / end); an empty data set shows the empty slot (default: emptyLabel, 'No items to show', one neutral statement in body/md content/subtle on the table's own surface, transparent like a passed Empty State).

Render the header when there's a title or description; render the toolbar for search/toolbarActions/actions/clear/active-filters or a selection; render the footer when pagination is enabled and there's more than one page or itemsPerPageOptions is set.
interactionRules: Checkbox = row selection. Never use a row click for selection; rows are not clickable.
Link = navigation/routing. If a value is an entity, it must be a Link; a single primary destination can also be a dedicated Link/action near the row's trailing edge.
Button = action. Use Buttons for operations that change state, not for plain navigation.
Interactive controls inside a row (links, buttons, menus, checkboxes) behave independently and never trigger another row-level interaction.
Identifier typography: strong (heading weight, or a strong Link) for the name / first-column identifier; default (body weight, or a default Link) for every other column.
compositionRules: Give the table an accessible name via `caption` or `title`.
Pass a real `getRowId` whenever `selectable` (or sorting/pagination reorder rows).
Compose rich cells with `column.render` (Tag, Avatar, Link, Button, ...); keep them accessible.
Mark the identifier column with `emphasis: 'strong'` (and, if it routes, a `<Link emphasis="strong">`); leave other columns at body weight / default Links.
Provide `bulkActions` (Buttons) for the selection bar when `selectable`.

Pass filter/configure Icon Buttons through `toolbarActions`; pass `activeFilters` a Chip Group named with aria-label ('Active filters') holding Chip mode='filter'; drive filter state from the consumer.
Set a controlled `page` back to 1 when the search or a filter changes `data`.
Show a status in words with Label (its tones mean something); Badge is for counts of one to four characters.
For large/server datasets, use manualSort + manualPagination and fetch on the callbacks.
contentRules: Header labels are short noun phrases; align numeric columns to the end.
Keep the title a short phrase and the description one line.
responsiveRules: The grid scrolls horizontally within its region on narrow viewports; the card and toolbar wrap.
Set explicit `column.width` / `minWidth` to control wrapping and horizontal scroll.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes - all colours use semantic tokens.
implementationNotes: Generic over the row type, written as a plain function component (React.memo would erase the generic).
Use CSS Modules + design tokens only; row/header heights and the selection column width are structural px (not token-gated).

Compose existing components: Text Field + Icon Button (search), Checkbox (selection), Button (Clear filters), Skeleton (loading), and Select + Icon Button (the footer). Filters (Chip) and actions are consumer-rendered.
No MUI. No Tailwind. No hardcoded colours, spacing, radius, or typography.
do: Give every table an accessible name (caption or title).
Use `render` to compose cell content from existing atoms/molecules.
Select rows with checkboxes; provide bulkActions for the selection bar.
Mark the identifier column emphasis='strong' (and a strong Link if it routes).
Use manualSort + manualPagination for server-driven data; pass a stable getRowId when selecting.
dont: Don't use a data table for a simple key/value layout or a card grid.
Don't make whole rows clickable - selection is checkbox-only and navigation is a Link/action.
Don't rely on index-based row ids with selection when rows can reorder.
Don't bake domain-specific filter logic into the table - pass filter/configure buttons via `toolbarActions` and Chip mode='filter' via `activeFilters`.
Don't forget an accessible name, or labels on in-cell action controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a semantic role=table named by caption/title; columns render row[key] by default or column.render.
Sortable headers cycle asc/desc/none, set aria-sort, and reorder data client-side (unless manualSort, which only fires onSortChange).
selectable adds a Checkbox column with a header select-all that goes indeterminate; selection is controllable and checkbox-only (rows are not clickable).
Selecting rows shows the selection bar (count + bulkActions); every row shows a neutral-overlay hover; a lone row drops its bottom divider.
Columns resize via a role=separator header handle (pointer drag + Arrow keys); resizableColumns=false / column.resizable=false opt out.
column.emphasis='strong' renders the cell at the heading weight.

pageSize paginates client-side; manualPagination shows pageCount pages with the range placed by page and pageSize; the footer stays while there are page sizes to pick; search works uncontrolled or controlled.

Every piece of built-in text (footer and its name, row Checkbox names, resize handle, default empty content, result count, scroll region fallback name) is a prop with an English default, so it can be translated.

loading shows skeleton rows (aligned like their columns) + aria-busy; an empty data set shows 'No items to show' by default; a changed result count is announced politely; an uncontrolled client-side page goes back to 1 on a new result set.
Composes className + data-size; uses only semantic tokens; works in light and dark themes.
Storybook includes Basic, Sortable, Selectable, Pagination, Sizes, WithToolbar, Loading, Empty, and FullShell.

Tests cover render/default+custom cell, sort (client + manual), selection + select-all/indeterminate + checkbox-only, selection bar, resize handles, emphasis, client pagination, loading, empty, search, and size/className.
knownLimitations: Single-select (radio) column, the per-column ⋮ menu, column reorder, sticky first column, and row expansion are deferred (the Figma page is still in-progress).
The built-in client-side sort compares row[key] (or column.sortValue) with a general comparator; complex/locale-specific sorts need manualSort.
Resized column widths are session-only state (not persisted) and reset on remount.
No row groups: grouped rows (a roadmap's stages) are separate tables, each with its own scroll region (and tab stop) and its own `activeFilters`. A designed boundary until the Roadmap designs land.
futureEnhancements: Single-select (radio) rows and the per-column options menu.
Column reorder, a sticky first column, and persisted column widths.
